findings.area: A02 root-contract, C1 capability axis (claims-as-enforced that are not enforced)
findings.claim: root-contract section 3 lists symlink_policy default reject under the bold marker for an enforced rule, and section 5 asserts as verified fail-closed behaviour: omitting it means symbolic links are rejected, marked with a check symbol and keep as-is.
findings.counter_evidence: Repo-wide grep for the only consumer pattern returns parsing and defaults but no enforcement: config.py L79 (allowed field list) and L140 (parse with default), models.py L101 (dataclass default), policy_2x.py L39 and L164 (same parse), plus five test files that only assert the parsed value. Grep for is_symlink, symlink or reparse across the whole wiki source tree returns zero hits, and symlink_policy appears in no scanner, resolver, service, reader, or store module. Command: Get-ChildItem company-wiki -Recurse -Include *.py | Select-String -Pattern 'symlink_policy' ; Select-String -Path <source_catalog/*.py> -Pattern 'is_symlink|reparse'. The field is stored and never read, so omission cannot reject anything.
findings.required_fix: Reclassify symlink_policy as declared-but-unenforced and remove it from the enforced column of C1 and from the fail-closed list in section 5. Either implement and cite the enforcement site, or record it as a capability gap requiring a VR negative test that proves the real behaviour on a symlinked path.

findings.area: A02 root-contract, C4 reuse axis and the section 2 decision chain
findings.claim: root-contract section 2 freezes the reusable decision chain as reusable_root_kinds then is_canonical then priority, stating that the order is the semantics, and C4 presents reusable_for_filing as the root-level switch whose None value follows the kind policy. baseline-map section 1 additionally asserts a priority branch in resolver.py.
findings.counter_evidence: The chain as written does not exist. (a) resolver.py L782-786 builds reusable_root_ids as the set of roots whose kind is in reusable_root_kinds; reusable_for_filing is never consulted there or at the reuse gate at L933-940, which tests only item.get('root_id') in reusable_root_ids. Therefore an explicit reusable_for_filing: false on a directory-kind root cannot disable reuse in the resolver; that is fail-open with respect to an explicit false, the exact semantics execution-plan B01 requires to be preserved. (b) Select-String resolver.py -Pattern priority returns exactly one hit, L531, inside a string literal: the rationale dict value 'lowest_priority_active_original_primary_then_tiebreak'. That is a label, not a branch, so the claimed one priority branch is zero branches. (c) The per-root override is honoured only by policy_2x.py L308 _effective_reusable_2x, a private helper that is not in policy_2x.__all__, in a module with no production caller (see A-DR-03). (d) The real priority ordering lives in SQL: ORDER BY l.document_id, r.priority, l.root_id, l.relative_path at service.py L329 and again at L527.
findings.required_fix: Re-derive the reuse chain from resolver.py plus the service.py SQL and state plainly that root-level reusable_for_filing currently has no effect on the resolver reuse gate while kind membership does. Take an explicit A.DR and owner ruling on whether an explicit false must be honoured (fail-closed) before A02 is frozen, and correct the priority-branch claim in baseline-map section 1.

findings.area: A02 root-contract, TO-VERIFY item 3 (canonical_write_target) and duplicated config admission
findings.claim: root-contract section 3 C2 states that the write-target restriction itself is TO-VERIFY because no ownership validation for canonical_write_target was found, and defers it to VR as a required real-command test.
findings.counter_evidence: The stated negative is false and the item is statically answerable now. Enforcement exists: policy_2x.py L49 defines _WRITABLE_KINDS = frozenset({'company_raw'}) and L121-131 raises CatalogConfigError when a write target has a non-writable kind or when read_only is true; policy_3x.py L12 documents the same rule. The decisive fact the contract misses is that this check is not on the production admission path: cli.py L14 imports load_catalog_config from config.py and calls it at L868, and __init__.py L3 exports that same function, while a repo-wide grep for load_root_policy_2x finds callers only in policy_2x.py itself, policy_3x.py L95, and five test files. config.py allowed_root_fields (L75-81) omits cohort and canonical_write_target, so declaring a write target under the active loader raises unknown fields at L82-84 rather than being validated. Two divergent admission implementations now exist for the same YAML.
findings.required_fix: Delete the incorrect no-validation statement; record that canonical_write_target is enforced only by a non-production loader and is rejected outright by the active loader; and treat the coexistence of config.py and policy_2x.py admission rules as a finding against execution-plan section 4 (one source of permission rules), to be resolved before A02 is frozen.

findings.area: A03 operation-contract section 2.1 (command wrongly placed in the read-only list)
findings.claim: operation-contract section 2.1 places identify in the query_local candidate list with the remark pure identity resolution and, unlike duplicate-preview and activation preview, attaches no caveat or TO-VERIFY flag to it.
findings.counter_evidence: identify is flag-dependent and its refresh path performs network calls and local writes. cli.py L1080-1087: when args.refresh is set, identify constructs OfficialSecurityMasterRefresher(store).refresh(markets=...) before resolving. security_identity.py L20 imports requests; L26-L45 define https endpoints for cninfo, hkexnews and SEC or nasdaqtrader; L1007 performs requests.get; L348 performs temporary.write_text; L1047 defines def refresh. So identify --refresh is simultaneously N (network) and W (local write) and must not be reachable from query_local. Command: Select-String -Path security_identity.py -Pattern 'def refresh|requests|http|write_text'.
findings.required_fix: Split the command by flag: identify without --refresh may remain R subject to VR; identify --refresh moves out of query_local into the request_work or higher-authority class, and the split must be added to the section 2.3 high-risk list because the plan's A03 rebuttal rule is triggered by exactly this kind of hidden ensure or refresh path.

findings.area: A03 operation-contract command inventory (incomplete surface, the plan's named forbidden action is absent)
findings.claim: operation-contract section 2 presents the CLI command mapping as the basis for query_local versus request_work, section 2.2 lists worker as the only system or background command, and baseline-map and findings claim the 47-subcommand surface was measured.
findings.counter_evidence: The 47 leaf count is right but the enumeration is not: 7 leaf commands are missing, and the arithmetic closes exactly (40 enumerated plus 7 missing equals 47). The AST parse of cli.py shows that add_worker_control_parser at L578 creates parsers through subparsers.add_parser(name, help=help_text) at L579, and it is invoked at L587, L592, L598 and twice in the loop at L604-608, producing worker-status, worker-start, worker-resume, worker-pause and worker-stop. All five are dispatched in main: worker-status L1405, worker-start L1479, worker-resume L1484, worker-pause L1489, worker-stop L1494. The other two omissions are derived-audit, dispatched at L972, and import-portfolio, dispatched at L1336, whose help text is promote already-indexed dayu-portfolio documents into company_raw canonical sources, i.e. a canonical write. worker-pause and worker-resume are precisely the pause-worker action that A03's own rule R3 names as a reason to reject a pure-query design, so the operation contract omits the commands most material to its own gate.
findings.required_fix: Add all seven commands with their own help text and side-effect class, determine read versus write for derived-audit from its handler (it calls reconcile_artifacts with the catalog database path at L976-980), and place the worker-control family in the system class with the note that none of them may be reachable from query_local or open_version.

findings.area: A01 baseline-map subprocess inventory, and findings F-A01-2 evidence quality
findings.claim: baseline-map section 1 gives a subprocess list of cross-repo spawn points consisting of filing fetch_filing.py, revenue source_preparation.py, one unattributed line saying the wiki ensure command starts subprocesses per provider, plus legacy_observer and daily_t2_runner which are declared not on the chain. findings F-A01-2 cites revenue scripts/company_wiki_source.py lines 12 and 261, routed through filing_fetch_client.resolve_filing, as evidence that the cross-repo main chain is a subprocess cascade.

findings.area: A04 identity-contract rule R4 and TO-VERIFY item V3
findings.claim: identity-contract section 1 freezes rule R4, that path diagnostic information must not enter business identity, so root_id and relative path are used only for location and diagnostics and never as a criterion for sameness. Section 4 V3 defers the question of whether the is_canonical selection key uses only path or priority to a TO-VERIFY requiring a read-only database query, framed as a search for residue.
findings.counter_evidence: The residue is already determinable from source and it is present. The location ordering that drives canonical and primary selection sorts by root priority, then root_id, then relative path: ORDER BY l.document_id, r.priority, l.root_id, l.relative_path at service.py L329 and again at L527. resolver.py L912-921 additionally filters canonical candidate locations by relative-path content, excluding any path containing .rejections, and L528-533 publishes the rationale string lowest_priority_active_original_primary_then_tiebreak. Priority and path therefore participate in choosing which location represents a document today, which is the opposite of R4 as stated. Command: Select-String -Path service.py,store.py,scanner.py -Pattern 'ORDER BY' -Context 0,3.
findings.required_fix: State R4 as a target rather than a current fact and name the existing residue (priority, root_id and relative path in the location ordering, plus the .rejections path filter). Answer the static half of V3 now from service.py and resolver.py, and keep only the genuinely data-dependent half in VR.

findings.area: Boundary claim versus filesystem evidence (declared no database access)
findings.claim: baseline-map section 0 and section 5, identity-contract section 6 and task_plan declaration state that no CLI was executed, no product file, config, DB, task or network was touched, and identity-contract explicitly says the catalog database was not accessed. checkpoint.json records actual_side_effects as none, no CLI executed, no product file/data/DB/network/task touched.
findings.counter_evidence: The production catalog SQLite shared-memory file was modified inside the run window. catalog.sqlite3-shm has LastWriteTime 2026-09-11 21:18:15, which is 1 minute 21 seconds after checkpoint.json was written at 21:16:54 and about 12 minutes after the first run-dir document at 21:06:05. Enumerating every file under .source_catalog modified on or after 2026-09-11 returns exactly that one file. A WAL shared-memory file is created or updated when a connection opens a WAL-mode database, and the catalog is addressed as catalog_dir/catalog.sqlite3 with catalog_dir ${PROJECT_ROOT}/.source_catalog. Attribution limit stated honestly: this evidences a connection, not necessarily a logical write, and I cannot prove which process opened it. No wiki worker log under .source_catalog is newer than 2026-08-20 and the newest non-database artifact there is legacy_periods.json at 2026-09-10 22:00:13, which is consistent with the 22:00 daily job rather than with activity at 21:18. The queried logon task company-wiki-source-catalog-worker does not exist on this machine (schtasks returned the system cannot find the file specified), so a scheduled logon-task start is not the explanation. Command: Get-Item .source_catalog/catalog.sqlite3* ; Get-ChildItem .source_catalog -Recurse -File -Force | Where-Object { $_.LastWriteTime -ge 2026-09-11 } ; schtasks /query.
findings.required_fix: The author must explain the 21:18:15 connection and, if it originated in the authoring session, correct the read-only declaration and the checkpoint side-effect field. For the gate, replace self-declaration with an independent operator observation of open handles or an OS-level file-audit trail covering the window, because section 2 of the plan and handbook item 09 require an independent no-side-effect boundary rather than an author assertion. Note for scope discipline that this database is 49,677,344,768 bytes, so unintended opens are not cost-free.

findings.claim: checkpoint.json sets last_completed_step to A01 baseline map plus A02, A03 and A04 read-only drafts, and current_gate to A.DR package ready for submission, while task_plan.md records A02, A03 and A04 as not started and progress.md's final entry says the next step is to do the A02 design document.

Handbook section 2 items 02 and 12 make distinguishing plan from actual result a per-handover obligation.

findings.claim: Section 2.1 supports its provisional read-only classification with help-text columns, giving identity-enrichment preview the summary read-only: which assertions would flip and marking it as self-declared read-only, giving activation preview only a bare preview note and a VR flag, and marking extraction-quality as self-declared read-only.
findings.counter_evidence: The AST-extracted help strings do not match. identity-enrichment preview at cli.py L277 has help text preview a candidate assertion without writing. activation preview at L639 has help text read-only: which assertions would flip. extraction-quality at L366 has help text assess deterministic source/extraction quality without span bodies, which contains no read-only claim; size-report at L361 is the only one of these that self-declares read-only. So two help strings are swapped between rows and one self-declaration is attributed where it does not exist. The conclusions happen to survive, but the evidence column is the part VR is told to re-check.
findings.required_fix: Correct the help-text and self-declaration columns from the parser source, and drop the self-declared qualifier where the help text does not contain it.

findings.area: Gate artifacts required at this point in the plan
findings.claim: checkpoint.json submits the A.DR package with produced_files limited to seven documents and directories, and task_plan describes the run directory as meeting handbook sections 2.5 and 3.
findings.counter_evidence: execution-plan section 50 in the plan body states that each future phase run directory needs at minimum task_plan, findings, progress, an input and command manifest, results and reviews. execution-handbook section 3 lists card.json, baseline.json, command-manifest.json, data-manifest.json, oracle/, tests/, evidence/, reviews/, checkpoint.json, rollback-contract.json and outcomes.json. The run contains no command manifest, no input manifest, and no reviews directory before this review created it; the deferral of the command manifest is argued in the documents from handbook items 5 and 8, which is defensible for argv, but the deferral is recorded only in prose and not as a gate item. execution-plan section 3 item 3 also requires recording actual input dirty, config, schema and dependency hashes; baseline-map section 0 records the three HEADs, dirty counts and twelve file hashes but no dependency or lockfile hash and no schema hash, so the input freeze is narrower than the rule requires.
findings.required_fix: Add an input manifest carrying dependency and lockfile hashes and the catalog schema version, and either supply a command-manifest skeleton marked pending approval or record its absence explicitly in checkpoint failed_or_unknown and authorization_needed rather than leaving the minimum-artifact list unmet without a gate entry.

findings.area: A03 operation-contract section 2 axis definition (write versus egress conflation)
findings.claim: Section 2 defines axis X as outward transmission covering LLM, external services and export to an external location, and assigns export, policy-export and archive-retired-evidence to it.
findings.counter_evidence: None of the three sends content outward. cli.py L970-971 routes export and policy-export to _run_export_command, which writes into CatalogConfig.export_dir, defined at models.py L206-208 as catalog_dir/index, a local path. archive-retired-evidence at cli.py L1126-1132 writes gzip JSONL under project_root/source_manifests, also local. Labelling these as egress blurs the exact boundary the plan requires to be kept separate, since A02 axis C3 is content leaving to an external LLM or service and execution-plan section 9 requires reading capability, semantic validity, processing state and write or outbound permission to be held apart.
findings.required_fix: Split the axis into local write W and outward transmission X, move the three export commands to W, and reserve X for destinations that leave the machine or reach an external provider.

findings.area: A04 identity-contract rule R6 and its verification path cross-contract dependency
findings.claim: identity-contract section 2 states rule R6, that identity alias migration must keep old references resolvable or retain a mapping table, and section 4 V5 proposes verifying it with an identify read-only call plus an alias-table structure review.
findings.counter_evidence: R6 is normative only: it names no owner, no mechanism, no storage location and no acceptance test, so it cannot be frozen as a contract clause whose violation is detectable. Its proposed verification is also unsafe as written, because A03 section 2.1 lists identify as read-only while cli.py L1083-1087 shows the --refresh form performs network access and writes (see A-DR-04); a VR command built from V5 as phrased could cross the network boundary the run forbids.
findings.required_fix: Give R6 an owner, a mechanism and a concrete negative test, and constrain V5's command to the no-refresh form of identify explicitly so the verification cannot reach the refresher.

findings.claim: root-contract section 1 states that the admission validation for root_id and kind lives at config.py lines 70-118.

findings.area: Review-format requirement versus runtime capability (applies to this review)
findings.claim: execution-plan section 21 and execution-handbook section 3 require real task or agent IDs for review records and state that name strings do not count as passing.
findings.counter_evidence: The reviewer runtime exposes no tool that returns the caller's own agent identity; the only authoritative value available to me was the managed environment variable DSH_SESSION_ID, read as 7cd316cc-50bc-44d5-9574-180030d9ee09. A value the reviewer reports about itself is not independent evidence of independence, whatever its source.
findings.required_fix: Have the orchestrator or operator stamp the reviewer assignment into the checkpoint from outside the reviewer session, so the run ledger records an ID that the reviewer did not self-supply.

verdict_reason: Phase A cannot be accepted as a frozen design basis. The positive core is real and reproducible: all twelve A01 input hashes and byte sizes match, the three HEADs and the config root table match, the checkpoint's seven produced-file hashes match byte-for-byte, the cross-repo spawn citations for filing fetch_filing.py L199-L213 and revenue source_preparation.py L18 and L99 are accurate, the 47 leaf-command count and the two-level CLI structure are correct, and the declared boundaries of repository and directory isolation hold with nothing written into product code, configuration or the audit-evidence directory. But eight P1 findings go to the substance of the contracts rather than to presentation. A02 presents symlink_policy as an enforced fail-closed rule when no production code reads the field; it freezes a reusable decision chain that does not exist, because resolver.py L782-786 and L933-940 key reuse on kind membership and never consult reusable_for_filing, so an explicit false cannot disable reuse; its single priority branch is a string literal at resolver.py L531 while the real ordering is SQL at service.py L329 and L527; and it states that no canonical_write_target validation exists when enforcement does exist at policy_2x.py L49 and L121-131 on a loader with no production caller, while the active loader config.py rejects the field outright, leaving two divergent admission implementations exactly where the plan demands one source of permission rules. A03 places identify in the read-only list although cli.py L1083-1087 plus security_identity.py L20, L1007 and L348 make identify --refresh a network and write path; and its command enumeration covers 40 of 47 leaf commands, omitting worker-pause, worker-resume, worker-start, worker-stop, worker-status, derived-audit and import-portfolio, which means the operation contract omits the very pause action its own rule R3 names as a reason to reject a pure-query design. A01 asserts the cross-repo cascade partly on docstring text at company_wiki_source.py L3, L12 and L261 and reduces the wiki-side subprocess surface, which actually spans seven modules and at least twelve call sites including an external provider CLI in dayu_cli_adapter.py, to one unattributed line. A04's rule R4 is contradicted by the current selection key, which orders by root priority, root_id and relative path, and its V3 defers a question that source reading already answers. And the declared no-database boundary is contradicted by a production catalog SQLite shared-memory write at 2026-09-11 21:18:15, inside the run window and after the checkpoint was written. Because these defects are false enforcement claims, an incomplete side-effect surface, and an unexplained boundary event rather than minor citation slips, the design is not safe to freeze or to build phase B on. Rejection is a statement about the design basis, not about the honesty of the run; the documents are unusually explicit about their own uncertainty, which is what makes the remaining false-verified claims material.
resubmission_path: Revisions that would let A.DR pass on a second pass: (1) correct every enforcement claim to the enforcement site or reclassify it as a gap, specifically symlink_policy and the reuse axis; (2) re-derive the reuse chain and the canonical selection key from resolver.py and the service.py SQL rather than from symbol hits, and obtain the owner ruling on explicit reusable_for_filing false; (3) resolve the two-loader divergence and delete the incorrect canonical_write_target negative; (4) split identify by flag and add the seven missing commands so the operation surface is complete; (5) rebuild the A01 subprocess table per module with line numbers and remove docstring citations; (6) restate A04 R4 as a target with the named residue and answer V3's static half; (7) reconcile task_plan, progress and checkpoint including pending_review and the re-frozen HEAD; (8) explain or correct the 21:18:15 catalog connection and support the boundary claim with an independent observation rather than self-declaration; (9) add the input manifest and either a command-manifest skeleton or an explicit gate entry for its absence. Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 require no execution and no data access, so they do not need the owner's data-read permission.
